covers.quote: All reports have a landing page or cover (if printed).
The landing page or cover also shows the:
title
subtitle, if any
name of the author or editor.

rules.quote: Use the landing page or cover to identify the report
rules.violation_condition: A report lacks a landing page or printed cover identifying its title, applicable subtitle, and author or editor.
when: Use a landing page for an online report and a cover for a printed report.
A subtitle is required only if the report has one.
The date and publisher are optional here.
rules.why: G-4: the body supplies the identification information meant by the heading; optional details are exceptions, not additional rules.

rules.quote: Use these to give an overview of the report so people can decide if they want to download or read it.
rules.specification: Assess whether the landing page or cover conveys the report's subject and scope. This is distinct from merely displaying its identification details.
rules.violation_condition: The landing page or cover provides no overview sufficient to help a reader decide whether to download or read the report.
when: Applies to an online report's landing page or a printed report's cover.
rules.why: G-4: the body states an overview requirement distinct from the identification-details check.

covers.quote: Electronic versions must be identical to printed versions and must be accessible.

rules.quote: Australian Government reports published online should include the same information as a printed version.
rules.specification: Compare textual information across versions. General online reports should contain the same information; versions subject to the parliamentary requirement must have identical text. The separate accessibility requirement is not part of this check.
rules.violation_condition: An online report and its printed counterpart contain different information, or parliamentary electronic and printed versions have different text.
when: A printed counterpart exists.
For parliamentary documents covered by the printing requirements, equivalence is mandatory and the versions must be identical.
rules.why: G-2: consolidate version-equivalence requirements while preserving the stronger parliamentary condition.

covers.quote: title
subtitle, if any
author’s name
name of the sponsor, if applicable.

rules.quote: A title page should include the following:
rules.violation_condition: A title page omits the report title, an existing subtitle, the author's name, or an applicable sponsor's name.
when: A subtitle is required only if there is one.
A sponsor's name is required only if applicable.
Other contributor details are optional.
rules.why: G-2: the list defines one title-page completeness check, with conditional fields.

covers.quote: You can put information prepared for the reverse title page somewhere else such as the inside front cover or back cover, if you’re not leaving those blank.

rules.quote: Wherever it features, people should be able to easily find copyright and other information about the report.
rules.specification: The page does not define an objective test for 'easily find' or an exhaustive set of 'other information'. Do not require a particular page location.
rules.violation_condition: Copyright and other report information is presented in a location or structure that makes it difficult to find.
when: Imprint information may appear on an imprint page, splash screen, landing page or another permitted location.
rules.why: G-3: alternative locations are permissions; the check concerns findability rather than a compulsory imprint-page location.

rules.quote: Show the main title exactly as it appears on the cover.
rules.violation_condition: The main title on a half-title page differs from the main title on the cover.
when: The printed report has a half-title page.
A half-title page is optional.
rules.why: G-3: optional half-title pages have requirements when present; their optional existence is not a separate rule.

rules.quote: Do not show any subtitles.
rules.violation_condition: A half-title page includes a subtitle.
when: The printed report has a half-title page.
rules.why: G-1: retain this specific half-title convention independently of the preliminary-content section.

rules.quote: Include a series title if the report is part of a series.
rules.violation_condition: The half-title page of a report in a series omits the series title.
when: The printed report has a half-title page.
The report belongs to a series.
rules.why: G-2: series membership is the condition for this inclusion check.

examples.note: Examples of the required lower case roman numeral forms.

rules.quote: Number them with lower case roman numerals such as ’i’, ’ii’, ’iii’ and ’iv’.
rules.violation_condition: Printed preliminary pages are unnumbered or numbered using a form other than lower case roman numerals.
when: Applies to preliminary pages in printed reports.
rules.why: G-4: use the specific numbering sentence, not the preceding instruction to check the order.

covers.quote: It must have:
the signature of the person responsible for the report
the day, month and year the report was submitted.

rules.quote: The letter of transmittal must include the purpose of the report and who it is for.
rules.violation_condition: A letter of transmittal omits the report's purpose, intended recipient, responsible person's signature, or submission date including day, month and year.
when: The report includes a letter of transmittal.
This page does not specify all circumstances in which a letter must be included.
rules.why: G-2: consolidate the required elements into one letter-of-transmittal completeness check.

covers.quote: A foreword:
A preface:
is always in the preliminary content

rules.quote: is always in the preliminary content
rules.violation_condition: A foreword or preface is placed outside the report's preliminary content.
when: The report has a foreword or preface.
The page does not require every report to have either.
rules.why: G-2: forewords and prefaces are two cases of the same placement check.

covers.quote: can be in the preliminary content or main part of the report

rules.quote: should be in the main part of the report if people will need the content to understand the report – for example, if the introduction includes terms of reference
rules.violation_condition: An introduction containing information needed to understand the report is placed in the preliminary content rather than the main body.
when: The introduction contains information needed to understand the report.
Otherwise, an introduction may be in the preliminary content or main body.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3: essential content triggers the placement check; the general choice of location is a permission.

covers.quote: An introduction:

rules.quote: does not include a signature
rules.violation_condition: The report's introduction includes a signature.
when: Applies to an introduction, not a foreword, preface or letter of transmittal.
rules.why: G-1: retain the explicit no-signature convention rather than turning the whole description of introductions into a rule.

rules.quote: Use the heading ‘Contents’, not ‘Table of contents’ or ‘List of contents’.
rules.violation_condition: The contents list is headed ‘Table of contents’, ‘List of contents’ or another heading instead of ‘Contents’.
when: The report has a contents list.
rules.why: G-4: the body states the actionable heading convention.

rules.quote: There is rarely a need to use more than 3 levels of headings.
rules.specification: This is a qualified recommendation, not an absolute 3-level limit. The page does not define when additional levels are warranted.
rules.violation_condition: A contents list uses more than 3 heading levels without a need for the additional hierarchy.
when: Applies to heading levels displayed in the contents list.
Additional levels may be warranted in exceptional cases.
rules.why: G-2: preserve the qualification rather than inventing an absolute prohibition.

rules.quote: Include a list of images and tables if it is helpful to the user.
rules.specification: The page supplies no objective threshold for when a list is helpful. Do not require one merely because any image or table is present.
rules.violation_condition: A report omits a list of images and tables despite readers needing such a list to locate them.
when: A list would be helpful to the report's users.
Images may include photographs, figures and maps.
rules.why: G-2: usefulness limits the inclusion requirement.

covers.quote: In print, include even full-page images that don’t have a visible page number.

rules.quote: Give each image a page number in the list.
rules.violation_condition: An image lacks a page-number reference in the report's image list, including a printed full-page image whose page number is not visible.
when: The report has an image list and page numbering.
In print, full-page images must be included even when their page number is not visible.
rules.why: G-2: full-page images are an explicit case of the image-reference completeness check.

covers.quote: photographs (only in print)
figures
maps (if listed separately)
tables.

rules.quote: The order of lists is:
rules.violation_condition: Separate image and table lists occur in an order other than photographs, figures, separately listed maps, then tables, after omitting categories not present.
when: The report has separate lists for these categories.
The photographs list applies only in print.
Maps need a separate position only if listed separately.
rules.why: G-2: the ordered items define one list-sequence check with conditional categories.

rules.quote: For long reports, use a summary to present findings, recommendations and conclusions.
rules.specification: The page does not define 'long'. Do not invent a page-count or word-count threshold.
rules.violation_condition: A long report lacks a summary presenting its findings, recommendations and conclusions.
when: The report is long.
The summary presents findings, recommendations and conclusions that the report contains.

anchor.quote: Where numbering restarts for each volume, references should include both the volume and page number.
anchor.suffix: Where the numbering continues a

covers.prefix: oth the volume and page number.
covers.quote: Where the numbering continues across volumes, use just the page number for the reference.

tags.violation_condition: A page reference omits the volume number when page numbering restarts by volume, or includes a volume number when page numbering is continuous across volumes.

when: Applies to references to pages in printed multi-volume reports.
Restarted numbering requires volume and page identifiers.
Continuous numbering requires only the page identifier.
rules.why: G-2: the numbering scheme changes the identifiers required by one page-reference check.
